Done. Full book, all ~3,875 lines, no gaps left. Here's the deep dive.

**The one-line verdict.** This is not a guide to revolution. It is a demolition manual for American ideology with a socialist horizon stapled to the end, and it is much better at the demolition than at the horizon.

**The machine.** The six chapters are one linked model, basically base and superstructure walked from the outside in: empire secures capitalist order abroad; liberals administer capitalism at home and convert every conflict into process; conservatives openly organize hierarchy and punishment; media converts elite access into unearned authority; culture substitutes symbolic representation for material power; wage labor disciplines everyone beneath the ruling class.

**Chapter by chapter, with the load-bearing bits.**

**Intro.** The joke platform (three-day week, free necessities, universal dogs, legal safe drugs, volcano punishment for the Iraq architects) establishes the book's rule: the first four are actual left demands, the volcano is catharsis. Read every joke in the book on this spectrum, payload plus noise.

**World.** Empire as protection racket: coups, dictators, proxy wars, military Keynesianism, Bretton Woods institutions as financial discipline. This is Lenin's *Imperialism* and Hobson in Chapo drag. Fine as a primer; the weakness is compression, multicausal history flattened into one clean class line.

**Libs.** The chapter that matters most for your politics. Liberalism borrows egalitarian language from the left but functions as capital's adaptive management layer. The New Deal: crisis relief that preserved capitalism and racial caste (this is Ira Katznelson's *Fear Itself* argument, uncited). Carter punctures the "Reagan started neoliberalism" myth, Volcker shock and deregulation under a Democrat. Clinton as executioner of the New Deal order: welfare reform, crime bill, Glass-Steagall repeal, NAFTA, telecom act, sanctions, DOMA/DADT. Obama: consensus chosen in a crisis, Clintonite staffing, finance protected, his own movement demobilized, filibuster preserved, drones and surveillance expanded. The neoliberalism intermission hides the book's best definition inside a Lovecraft joke: neoliberalism differs from classical liberalism by claiming political control of markets is not undesirable but *impossible*, markets as scientific forces outside human agency.

**Cons.** The strongest theoretical chapter. Freedom redefined as the superior's freedom to dominate the inferior. It explicitly rejects the liberal "duped Kansas voter" thesis: hierarchy delivers real goods, status, whiteness, the cathartic sadism of conquest. This is Corey Robin's *The Reactionary Mind* (2011) without the citation. The intellectual-tradition section does real pedagogical work between jokes: the genuinely informative point that the Moral Majority mobilized over segregated schools' tax exemptions, not *Roe*; the Rand Collective to Greenspan pipeline; Rothbard on children as property; Hoppe quoted directly on abolishing democracy and physically expelling dissidents. The Flintstone and Paul Kersey entries are pure noise. Trump as culmination, not rupture.

**Media.** Careerism as the theory of the press. The Iraq case: supporting the war as a credential, failing upward. The blogosphere history is the best-reported section in the book, genuinely footnoted: Sullivan's 9/11 bloodlust quoted verbatim, Little Green Footballs' pivot and post-scrubbing, Moulitsas's 2016 decay, Klein's own 2004 confession that hawkishness was about "seriousness," McArdle's Jane Galt archive (Iraq cost denial, calling for protesters to be beaten, the Sandy Hook human-wave column). The thesis: Vox as the institutional form of liberal-hawk careerism. Prestige TV section is good media sociology, the recap economy as the critical form of an exhausted audience, "ice cream for dinner." The gaming chapter's manuscript-hack is a formal joke about the book's own audience; the fake history (Ada Lovelace's *Cholera Quest*) is noise, the industry critique is sincere.

**Work.** The Lafargue epigraph (*The Right to Be Lazy*) tells you the lineage. "Work builds character," "the rich work hardest," "job creators" each get demolished; the one-line core: no employer hires unless they extract more value than wages cost. Enclosure as the origin of the wage relation, told as jokes with the mechanism intact. The jobs taxonomy, marketing/finance/law enforcement/academia as the jobs you'll never have, service/content/gig-serfdom/camming/tweet-replier/bio-bag as the jobs you will, is the book's funniest sustained stretch and also its bleakest. The fun-office as colonization of free time, an inversion of emancipation. The affirmative ending finally states the program: seize billionaire wealth, socialize it, worker control, automation down to a three-hour day, public healthcare/education/science/infrastructure.

**Epilogue.** The left's 20th-century destruction (raids, McCarthyism, COINTELPRO, Taft-Hartley, purges into sects or academia); coming catastrophes economic, automated, climatic; against consumer escape and permanent online rage; the prescription is a disposition, "good-humored, thick-skinned, maybe even optimistic struggle"; final line, socialism or drowning in boiling seawater.

**Sincerity map.** Irony is delivery infrastructure, not uncertainty. The durable claims are sincerely anti-capitalist, anti-imperialist, anti-neoliberal, pro-labor, and hostile to liberal proceduralism. The dirtbag performance does three jobs: refuses liberal civility norms, builds in-group solidarity, gives earnestness plausible deniability. Where the jokes are noise: the Lovecraft bit, Flintstone/Kersey, most fake gaming history, the volcano. Where jokes *are* the argument: the taxonomies, the Sopranos mapping, "How to Win Fake Friends and Influence Nobody."

**Strongest reasoning.** Conservatism-as-hierarchy against voter-confusion condescension. Neoliberalism-as-impossibility. Media careerism and Iraq impunity, with receipts. Wage labor's moralization. Culture as sublimation. Each is a thesis you could defend in a seminar; the book just refuses the seminar's manners.

**Weakest, not grading on a curve.** The title is false advertising: no organization, no transition, no strategy. The theory of change is demystification plus morale. The liberal chapter flattens distinct things, failure, compromise, agreement, structural constraint, into one moral narrative; the Obama section is the worst offender. No racial capitalism: race saturates the narrative but is never theorized, and the book cribs arguments about the New Deal and racial caste without touching the literature. Russiagate, written pre-Mueller, treats the whole thing as liberal cope; the MSNBC-conspiracism critique was fair, but the factual record of Russian interference landed after, so separate the two claims. The affirmative program is materially specific and institutionally empty: "seize the money" is a slogan, not a transition. And in places the economic history runs on vibes, jokes substituting for mechanisms.

**Aged through 2026, labeled.** This is my best understanding from training, not verified reporting, so take the 2024-2026 specifics accordingly. Held up: the liberal-proceduralism critique; Trump-as-culmination reads stronger after a second term built on open hierarchy politics; the media business-model collapse (BuzzFeed News dead 2023, Vice bankrupt 2023, the layoff wave, the book called the model insolvent in 2018); automation arriving as labor discipline rather than liberation, which sharpens the book's "only under social ownership" condition into the central AI-era question. Dated: the 2018 media bestiary is period-specific; the Russiagate posture; the confidence of the 2018 left upsurge, since the 2020s delivered fragmentation instead of the ascending DSA-era left the book assumes; the pre-COVID labor analysis. The final prediction, socialism or boiling seawater: the 2020s have so far delivered neither pole, just managed decline plus climate damage. Intact as a moral claim; untested as a prediction.

**The Dan connection, grounded.** Your corpus puts your hard-left turn in 2019 at Bernie plus Chapo, which makes you almost exactly this book's target formation: the reader it was trying to arm. Your conjunction rule, building plus cultural literacy, is the book's own method: the references are load-bearing, the Sopranos mapping and the Sorkin critique do analytical work, not decoration. The media chapter is your Trump-era journalism shelf with the footnotes showing. The work chapter's service/content taxonomy sits on top of your own labor history. And the book's anti-proceduralism, its contempt for norms-talk, is your vertical-authority skepticism in print.

**The scoring fix.** Stop reporting divergence as an absolute number. Build a null distribution: sample 10,000 historical windows matched to the scored window on size, hour-of-day, and recipient mix, compute divergence for each, and report the current window as a percentile against that null. "0.71" becomes "97th percentile of comparable windows," which is interpretable, immune to feature-count inflation, and automatically handles the fact that you write differently to Tom at 2am than to Ally at noon. Second: baseline conditionally, per (recipient × hour-bin × message-type) cell with shrinkage toward the global mean for sparse cells. Most of what your instrument currently reads as state drift is recipient and topic drift. Third: group features into ~8 axes, compute axis scores, and aggregate with Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage Mahalanobis over the axes rather than Euclidean distance over raw z's — otherwise correlated features double-count and dimensionality alone pushes distance up.

**Pastes.** Don't tag them, split them. A paste is not a corrupted language sample, it's a different data type. Detect with char count, newline density, URL/markdown/timestamp patterns, capitalized-line-start ratio, and MinHash near-duplicate check against the corpus; exclude hits from the language channel entirely, and then count paste rate itself as a behavioral feature. Research-spiral pasting at 3am is real signal — it's just signal about behavior, not about syntax.

**The content layer, in rough order of signal-per-unit-effort.** Affect lexicons first because they're free and instant: VADER valence, NRC eight-emotion counts, and Warriner valence/arousal/dominance norms averaged per message. Arousal is your highest-value single new variable for stimulant discrimination; dominance tracks grandiosity. Then pragmatic stance: hedge ratio (tentative vs. certainty terms), deontic modal density (must/should vs. might/could), imperative rate via sentence-initial bare verbs, negation density, intensifier/booster rate, discourse-marker rate, and an absolutism index (always/never/completely/totally) — absolutism is well-attested as a state marker and is content-derived without being topic-bound. Then temporal orientation: past/present/future tense ratios, plus agentive vs. experiencer framing ("I did X" vs. "X happened to me"), which is a different variable from the raw pronoun counts you already have.

Scope of this delivery: the scoring core and the channel splitter. The
labeling hotkey, the `messages.native` metadata channel, lexicon
residualization, the four-prompt battery, and embeddings/perseveration are
not in this drop — see "Not built, deliberately" at the end.

Nothing in `labels.jsonl` was touched. No corrections were appended: the
false positives found below are a scoring defect, not a ground-truth error,
and writing inference-derived invalidations into the ground-truth file is a
decision that should be yours, not a side effect of a code change.

---

## New files

| file | what it does |
|---|---|
| `robust.py` | rank-to-probit scoring, quantile grids, hierarchical shrinkage, axis grouping, shrinkage covariance, Mahalanobis |
| `splitter.py` | routes every message to language / artifact / mechanical |
| `baseline2.py` | builds `baseline2.json` — conditional quantile baselines, tiered by correspondent |
| `nullspace.py` | builds `nullspace.json` — matched empirical null distributions |
| `scorer2.py` | v2 scoring path; cron-safe, headless, CSV export |
| `verify_replay.py` | replays the 284 stored windows + splitter fixtures |

`features.py`, `contrast.py`, `baseline.py`, `baseline_windows.py`,
`scorer.py` are unmodified. v1 and v2 can run side by side; `runs/*.jsonl`
stays append-only and v2 records are a superset of v1's fields.

## 1. Divergence is now a percentile against matched history

**Was:** `mean of top-5 |z|`, flag at `> 2.0` with `>= 2` features over 2σ.

**Problem:** the number was uninterpretable, the threshold was unowned, and
the statistic inflates mechanically with feature count — so the planned v2
feature expansion would have made the instrument worse on the old
aggregation. Measured on your own runs, `2.0` sits at the **88.7th
percentile** of observed windows: 28 flags in 284 windows, ~7/day.

**Now:** thousands of historical windows are drawn from the corpus, matched
to the scored window on `(recipient_tier, hour_bin, size_bin)`, pushed
through the identical scoring path, and the live window is reported as a
percentile of that distribution. Operating point is set in flags-per-day, not
in sigma. Default `--flag-percentile 0.995`.

The stratum actually used is written into every record (`null_stratum`,
`null_n`), so a percentile can never be read without knowing what it was
matched against. Lookup falls back
`(tier,hour,size) → (tier,size) → (size) → global` until a stratum has ≥200
draws.

**Replay result:** 28 flags → 2. ~7/day → ~0.5/day.

## 2. 29 features → 8 axes

Measured across the 284 stored windows:

```
n_chars ~ n_words   r = +0.990
n_chars ~ n_sents   r = +0.937
n_sents ~ n_words   r = +0.896
```

53.2% of windows had ≥2 of the length family in the top-5 drivers. The
divergence index was, more than half the time, measuring message length two
or three times and dividing by five.

Axes: `volume, shape, punctuation, expressivity, stance, deixis, lexical,
rhythm`. Axis score = signed mean of member probits, so collinear members
reinforce as one unit and opposed members cancel. `peak` and `peak_feature`
are retained per axis so a lone mover stays visible. `dash_p100` stays
excluded.

**Replay result:** of 48 windows whose top-3 drivers were *all* length-family,
22 flagged under v1, **2** under v2.

## 3. Rank-to-probit instead of median/MAD

The brief asked for median/MAD. MAD fails on this feature set: `excl_p100` is
nonzero in 1.6% of your messages, `emoji_p100` ~2%, `quest_p100` 6.4%. Any
feature that is zero in >50% of the corpus has MAD exactly 0 and robust z is
undefined or infinite.

Rank-to-probit maps a value to its percentile in the conditional baseline,
then through the inverse normal CDF. Zero-inflation safe, skew safe
(`burst_mph` is 38.5 ± 102), and **outlier-bounded by construction**: the
percentile is clamped to `1/(2n)` before the probit, so the 10k-char YouTube
paste that scored 12.35 cannot exceed ±3.8 on any single feature. The paste
confound is capped before the splitter even runs.

Cost: baselines store 201-point quantile grids rather than two moments.

## 4. Conditional, tiered baselines

**Was:** global + per-hour-of-day mean/std, correspondent ignored.

**Now:** cells are `(recipient_tier, hour_bin)`, 6 four-hour bins, shrunk up
the ladder `cell → tier → global` with weight `n/(n+k₀)`.

Tiering per your call: top-K=10 correspondents get their own tier, everyone
else pools to `longtail`. With 503 handles and one correspondent at ~45% of
lifetime volume, per-contact cells are un-estimable for the tail. Shrinkage
means a thin cell degrades smoothly to its tier and a near-empty one to
global — no cliff, no special cases.

Quantile grids are blended by averaging the quantile *functions*, which is
the 1-D Wasserstein barycenter: unlike averaging densities it cannot invent
bimodality that neither input had.

Live Muse windows pass `--tier muse`. Until a Muse-register baseline exists
that tier is absent, so it falls back to `longtail` and every record carries
`tier_fallback: true`. The mechanism is built; the Muse corpus is not.

## 5. Splitter: three channels, not a confound tag

Every message routes to exactly one of:

- **language** — authored in his register. Scored.
- **artifact** — pasted/quoted/structured. Not scored; its *volume* becomes a
  behavioral feature.
- **mechanical** — near-duplicate of prior authored input. Not scored; its
  *rate* becomes a behavioral feature.

Paste detection is a transparent additive score over inspectable evidence
(length percentile, newline density, URLs, markdown/code/table structure,
speaker labels, timecode density, capitalized line-start ratio against your
8.4% caps baseline, prose-punctuation density). No opaque model: there are no
paste labels either, and a black box inside a state instrument just moves the
calibration problem somewhere darker.

Duplicate detection is 64-bit simhash over 5-gram shingles for long text,
**token-set Jaccard ≥0.75 for messages under 40 tokens** — shingle simhash is
too brittle short, where editing one word of a 13-token message changes 5 of
its 9 shingles. Repeat avatar commands are caught either way. Pasted
artifacts are excluded from duplicate history, so pasting the same transcript
twice is an artifact event, not evidence of perseveration.

Every window is scored **both ways**. `paste_inflation_d` and
`paste_inflation_pct_points` report the difference; the raw-distance version
exists because the percentile saturates at 1.0 and a huge paste would
otherwise read as "no inflation" at the ceiling.

**This is the ordering guard for perseveration.** When the semantic layer
lands, max-cosine-against-previous-k must consume the language channel only.
If repeat commands reach it, the looping detector becomes a repeated-command
detector that fires hardest on exactly the repetitive-generation days you
would also expect to be stimulated — right answer, wrong reason, invisible
from inside the calibration.

3. **Short-message duplicate blindness.** See §5.

under the old absolute threshold it would have produced confident flags on

`calibration_strength()` counts high-confidence same-day labeled episodes per

misread as a v1 z.
